title: The Latest Showdown Over a Shutdown

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、佐兰·蒙达尼等许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily Mail.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日邮报》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日新闻。

sentences.en: Today, President Trump seemed poised to avoid a government shutdown and carry his fight for a border wall into 2019 with a Democratic-controlled House.
sentences.zh: 今天，特朗普总统似乎准备避免政府停摆，并打算在民主党控制众议院的情况下，将边境墙之争延续到2019年。

sentences.en: So what happened?
sentences.zh: 那么发生了什么？

sentences.en: And Jim Mattis has resigned as Secretary of Defense.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·马蒂斯已经辞去了国防部长一职。

sentences.en: It's Friday, December 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月21日，星期五。

sentences.en: Jonathan, it is 4.42 on Thursday afternoon.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，现在是周四下午4点42分。

sentences.en: Are we, again, facing a government shutdown?
sentences.zh: 我们是否又面临政府停摆了？

sentences.en: We are.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I came into work this morning thinking that it was going to be unpalatable, but the House Republicans were going to take up the Senate-passed bill
sentences.zh: 我今天早上来上班时，以为这会是一场令人不快的局面，但众议院共和党人会采纳参议院通过的法案，

sentences.en: that would have kept the government funded past Friday and punted it to February, and everyone would jump in their airplanes and leave Washington,
sentences.zh: 该法案本可以让政府在周五之后继续获得资金，并将问题推迟到二月，然后每个人都会跳上飞机离开华盛顿，

sentences.en: and we would be on our way to winter break, and we're not.
sentences.zh: 我们本该踏上寒假之旅，但现在并没有。

sentences.en: By my count, Jonathan, this would be our third government shutdown in- In a year.
sentences.zh: 据我统计，乔纳森，这将是我们一年内的第三次政府停摆。

sentences.en: In a year.
sentences.zh: 一年内。

sentences.en: In a year.
sentences.zh: 一年内。

sentences.en: And each one of them seems to center around the president, Chuck Schumer, and Nancy Pelosi arguing about a wall.
sentences.zh: 而且每一次似乎都围绕着总统、查克·舒默和南希·佩洛西关于建墙的争论。

sentences.en: In immigration, yes.
sentences.zh: 在移民问题上，是的。

sentences.en: Jonathan Weissman is Deputy Washington Editor of The Times.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森·韦斯曼是《时报》华盛顿分社副主编。

sentences.en: Remember, the last one was over the Democrats insisting on some kind of protection for the Dreamers, and that one actually went poorly for the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 记住，上一次停摆是因为民主党坚持要为“追梦人”提供某种保护，而那次对民主党来说实际上结果很糟糕。

sentences.en: The Democrats pretty much capitulated and lost on that one.
sentences.zh: 民主党在那次事件中几乎投降并输掉了。

sentences.en: So how did we get here all over again?
sentences.zh: 那么我们又是如何再次走到这一步的呢？

sentences.en: Well, remember, the actual fiscal year ended September 30th, and since then, we've been living on these stopgap spending bills that just keep the money flowing to the government.
sentences.zh: 嗯，记住，实际的财政年度在9月30日结束，从那时起，我们就一直靠这些临时支出法案维持政府资金运转。

sentences.en: Now, the last stopgap spending bill was supposed to end a few weeks ago, but then George H.W.
sentences.zh: 现在，上一个临时支出法案本应在几周前结束，但后来乔治·H·W·

sentences.en: Bush died, and we didn't want to have this kind of unseemly spectacle as we were celebrating the former president's life.
sentences.zh: 布什去世了，我们不想在纪念这位前总统生平的时候出现这种不体面的闹剧。

sentences.en: So they passed yet another short-term spending bill that pushed us to the edge of Christmas, and here we are.
sentences.zh: 所以他们又通过了一项短期支出法案，把我们推到了圣诞节的边缘，现在我们就在这里。

sentences.en: So what happens after George H.W.
sentences.zh: 那么在乔治·H·W·

sentences.en: Bush is laid to rest, the celebrations are over, and Washington does finally turn to the budget?
sentences.zh: 布什入土为安、纪念活动结束后，华盛顿最终转向预算问题时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Okay, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's a great honor to have Nancy Pelosi with us and Chuck Schumer with us.
sentences.zh: 非常荣幸能有南希·佩洛西和查克·舒默与我们在一起。

sentences.en: Well, that was a moment when President Trump summoned Nancy Pelosi, the expected next speaker, and Chuck Schumer, the Senate Minority Leader, to the White House.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是特朗普总统召集预计将成为下一任议长的南希·佩洛西和参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默到白宫时的一个时刻。

sentences.en: And then we have the easy one, the wall.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还有一个简单的议题，就是墙。

sentences.en: The wall?
sentences.zh: 墙？

sentences.en: That'll be the one that will be the easiest of all?
sentences.zh: 那会是最容易解决的一个吗？

sentences.en: What do you think, Chuck?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢，查克？

sentences.en: Maybe not?
sentences.zh: 也许不是？

sentences.en: It's called funding the government, Mr. President.
sentences.zh: 这叫为政府提供资金，总统先生。

sentences.en: So we're going to see, but I will tell you the wall will get built.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要拭目以待，但我可以告诉你，墙一定会建起来的。

sentences.en: Now, he relishes this.
sentences.zh: 现在，他很享受这一点。

sentences.en: He wanted to have a public fight over the wall right then.
sentences.zh: 他当时就想就建墙问题进行公开争论。

sentences.en: One way or the other, it's going to get built.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，它都会建起来的。

sentences.en: I'd like not to see a government closing, a shutdown.
sentences.zh: 我不希望看到政府关闭，即停摆。

sentences.en: We will see what happens over the next short period of time.
sentences.zh: 我们将看看在接下来的短时间内会发生什么。

sentences.en: But the wall is a very important thing to us.
sentences.zh: 但墙对我们来说是非常重要的事情。

sentences.en: The cameras are rolling.
sentences.zh: 摄像机正在拍摄。

sentences.en: This was supposed to be a closed-door negotiation.
sentences.zh: 这本应是一次闭门谈判。

sentences.en: And he starts negotiating right there in front of the cameras.
sentences.zh: 但他就在摄像机前开始谈判了。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter, though, because we can't get it passed in the Senate because we need 10 Democrat votes.
sentences.zh: 不过没关系，因为我们在参议院无法通过它，我们需要10张民主党的票。

sentences.en: That's the problem.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: Again, let us have our conversation, then we can meet with the press again.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，让我们先谈谈，然后我们再和媒体见面。

sentences.en: But the fact is, is that legislating, which is what we do, you begin...
sentences.zh: 但事实是，立法，也就是我们所做的事情，你开始……

sentences.en: The Democrats are looking around the corner.
sentences.zh: 民主党人正在未雨绸缪。

sentences.en: They want Donald Trump to take responsibility in case there is a shutdown coming.
sentences.zh: 他们希望如果真的发生停摆，唐纳德·特朗普能承担责任。

sentences.en: So they push him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们逼迫他。

sentences.en: 20 times you have called for, I will shut down the government if I don't get my wall.
sentences.zh: 你已经说了20次了，如果我拿不到建墙资金，我就让政府停摆。

sentences.en: None of us have said...
sentences.zh: 我们谁也没说……

sentences.en: You want to know something?
sentences.zh: 你想知道点什么吗？

sentences.en: And much to their surprise and delight, he says, yeah.
sentences.zh: 令他们惊讶和高兴的是，他说，是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If we don't get what we want, one way or the other, whether it's through you, through a military, through anything you want to call, I will shut down the government.
sentences.zh: 如果我们得不到我们想要的，不管通过什么方式，无论是通过你，通过军队，还是通过任何你想称呼的方式，我都会让政府停摆。

sentences.en: Okay, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 好的，绝对的。

sentences.en: And I am proud, and I'll tell you what, I am proud to shut down the government for border security, Chuck.
sentences.zh: 而且我很自豪，我告诉你，查克，我很自豪能为了边境安全而让政府停摆。

sentences.en: And John, why would the president happily, even proudly, own a shutdown?
sentences.zh: 约翰，为什么总统会乐意，甚至自豪地承担停摆的责任？

sentences.en: Something that historically, every politician is desperate to avoid and to point the finger at someone else for.
sentences.zh: 这在历史上是每位政治家都极力避免并试图指责他人的事情。

sentences.en: You know, Donald Trump looks at his core supporters, and his core supporters were the ones who were listening to him when he came down the escalator at Trump Tower,
sentences.zh: 你知道，唐纳德·特朗普看着他的核心支持者，当他在特朗普大厦乘坐自动扶梯下来时，听他讲话的正是这些核心支持者，

sentences.en: opened his campaign by saying that Mexico was not sending their beSt.
sentences.zh: 他开启竞选活动时说墨西哥派来的不是最好的人。

sentences.en: They were sending their rapists and their drug dealers.
sentences.zh: 他们派来的是强奸犯和毒贩。

sentences.en: He knows who the people are who are his unshakable supporters, and they care more about these immigration issues than anything else.
sentences.zh: 他知道谁是他坚定不移的支持者，他们比任何事情都更关心这些移民问题。

sentences.en: He was playing to them.
sentences.zh: 他是在迎合他们。

sentences.en: He wants them on his side, and he's looking ahead to Nancy Pelosi and a Democratic House, and he understands this really is his last moment.
sentences.zh: 他想让他们站在自己这边，他展望着南希·佩洛西和民主党控制的众议院，他明白这确实是他最后的时刻。

sentences.en: This is when he has to fight, and his supporters want to see him go down swinging.
sentences.zh: 这是他必须战斗的时候，他的支持者想看到他奋力一搏。

sentences.en: Well, then isn't this a totally deadlocked situation at this point?
sentences.zh: 那么，此时此刻这难道不是一个完全陷入僵局的局面吗？

sentences.en: If the president thinks shutting down the government over the wall might actually be good for him politically, and Schumer and Pelosi are telling him,
sentences.zh: 如果总统认为因建墙而让政府停摆在政治上对他实际上是有利的，而舒默和佩洛西却告诉他，

sentences.en: no way, we're not going to give in to you, doesn't that create a complete deadlock, and there's no place for anyone to go?
sentences.zh: 没门，我们不会向你屈服，这难道不会造成彻底的僵局，让双方都无路可走吗？

sentences.en: It looks like a complete deadlock because the Democrats have absolutely no incentive to give him that money.
sentences.zh: 这看起来确实是一个彻底的僵局，因为民主党人完全没有动力给他那笔钱。

sentences.en: He's not offering them anything.
sentences.zh: 他没有给他们任何东西。

sentences.en: Why in the world would they offer something back?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要提供回报呢？

sentences.en: But remember, you know, there are other actors here.
sentences.zh: 但记住，你知道，这里还有其他参与者。

sentences.en: In this case, the House Republicans, the Senate Republicans, they have been persuasive in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，众议院共和党人和参议院共和党人过去一直很有说服力。

sentences.en: They've been able to go to the president and say, look, Mr. President, it just doesn't work that way.
sentences.zh: 他们能够去告诉总统，看，总统先生，事情不是那样运作的。

sentences.en: You have to give in because you have no choice.
sentences.zh: 你必须让步，因为你别无选择。

sentences.en: And I think that's where we thought we were, that eventually they would talk him into it.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们当时就是这么想的，最终他们会说服他。

sentences.en: And that is what seemed to be happening as we started getting toward this deadline.
sentences.zh: 当我们接近这个最后期限时，情况似乎确实如此。

sentences.en: Sarah Huckabee Sanders comes out and she says, You know, at this point, the Senate's thrown out a lot of ideas.
sentences.zh: 萨拉·赫卡比·桑德斯出来说，你知道，在这一点上，参议院已经提出了很多想法。

sentences.en: We're disappointed in the fact that they've yet to actually vote on something and pass something.
sentences.zh: 我们对他们至今尚未对某事进行投票并通过感到失望。

sentences.en: So when they do that, we'll make a determination on whether or not we're going to sign that.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们这样做时，我们将决定是否签署该法案。

sentences.en: In the meantime, we're looking at every avenue available to us possible.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，我们正在寻找一切可能的途径。

sentences.en: The president's asked every one of his cabinet secretaries to look for funding that can be used to protect our borders.
sentences.zh: 总统已要求他的每一位内阁部长寻找可用于保护我们边境的资金。

sentences.en: You know, we don't have to get the wall money.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们不必非要拿到建墙的钱。

sentences.en: Right now, we can take money from other parts of the government.
sentences.zh: 现在，我们可以从政府的其他部门挪用资金。

sentences.en: At the end of the day, we don't want to shut down the government.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，我们不想让政府停摆。

sentences.en: We want to shut down the border from illegal immigration.
sentences.zh: 我们想阻止非法移民进入边境。

sentences.en: And we were all fairly sanguine about our Christmas breaks.
sentences.zh: 我们对圣诞假期都感到相当乐观。

sentences.en: Are there any senators in the chamber wishing to vote or change their vote?
sentences.zh: 参议院里有参议员希望投票或更改投票吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And in response to that kind of new openness, the Senate passes a short-term spending bill, right?
sentences.zh: 为了回应这种新的开放态度，参议院通过了一项短期支出法案，对吧？

sentences.en: All in favor, say aye.
sentences.zh: 赞成的请说“赞成”。

sentences.en: Aye.
sentences.zh: 赞成。

sentences.en: Those opposed, no.
sentences.zh: 反对的，请说“反对”。

sentences.en: The ayes appear to have it.
sentences.zh: 赞成者似乎占多数。

sentences.en: The ayes do have it.
sentences.zh: 赞成者确实占多数。

sentences.en: The motion is agreed to.
sentences.zh: 动议获得通过。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, you would not think that Mitch McConnell, who is a wily guy, would have gone and put a bill to keep the government funded past Friday night into February
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你不会认为米奇·麦康奈尔这个精明的人会提出一项让政府在周五晚上之后继续获得资金直到二月的法案，

sentences.en: if he did not believe that Donald Trump would sign it.
sentences.zh: 如果他不相信唐纳德·特朗普会签署的话。

sentences.en: He's not that stupid.
sentences.zh: 他没那么蠢。

sentences.en: So I think that we were pretty sure he was going to sign this bill.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们相当确定他会签署这项法案。

sentences.en: Regardless of Republican pressure, why would he even consider a compromise?
sentences.zh: 撇开共和党的压力不谈，他为什么要考虑妥协？

sentences.en: Because the Democrats take control of the House in a week or two.
sentences.zh: 因为民主党在一两周内就要控制众议院了。

sentences.en: So doesn't it become exponentially more hard for the president to ever get his wall funded?
sentences.zh: 那么总统获得建墙资金的难度难道不会呈指数级增加吗？

sentences.en: Logically, you would think it's now or never.
sentences.zh: 从逻辑上讲，你会认为现在是最后的机会。

sentences.en: The Republicans are still in charge.
sentences.zh: 共和党人仍然掌权。

sentences.en: This is the only time you've got to get this wall.
sentences.zh: 这是你获得这堵墙的唯一机会。

sentences.en: But there's this other thing whispering in Donald Trump's ear, which is, remember, Nancy Pelosi goes to him at the White House and says, hey, you're in control.
sentences.zh: 但还有另一件事在唐纳德·特朗普耳边低语，那就是，记住，南希·佩洛西在白宫对他说了，嘿，你掌握着控制权。

sentences.en: The Republicans control the White House.
sentences.zh: 共和党人控制着白宫。

sentences.en: They control the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他们控制着参议院。

sentences.en: They control the House.
sentences.zh: 他们控制着众议院。

sentences.en: It's up to you to fund the government.
sentences.zh: 为政府提供资金取决于你。

sentences.en: Well, Mitch McConnell or some other Republican whispers in his ear and says, hey, if we just punt this into February, she doesn't have that argument.
sentences.zh: 嗯，米奇·麦康奈尔或其他共和党人在他耳边低语说，嘿，如果我们只是把这个问题推迟到二月，她就没有这个论点了。

sentences.en: Now you're having your wall fight with Nancy Pelosi.
sentences.zh: 现在你要和南希·佩洛西进行建墙之争了。

sentences.en: Isn't that better than having it with Paul Ryan and Mitch McConnell?
sentences.zh: 这难道不比和保罗·瑞安以及米奇·麦康奈尔争论更好吗？

sentences.en: And everyone thought that was what he had been sold on.
sentences.zh: 每个人都认为这就是他被说服的原因。

sentences.en: Let's have the wall fight with Nancy Pelosi.
sentences.zh: 让我们和南希·佩洛西进行建墙之争吧。

sentences.en: But Jonathan, isn't it still the case that as appealing as the optics of that fight might feel to some Republicans,
sentences.zh: 但是乔纳森，难道不是仍然存在这种情况吗？尽管这场争斗的视觉效果对一些共和党人来说可能很有吸引力，

sentences.en: that Trump would still lose that fight because the House will be controlled by Democrats?
sentences.zh: 但特朗普仍然会输掉这场争斗，因为众议院将由民主党控制？

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，绝对的。

sentences.en: The reason he can't win the fight now is he still needs 60 votes in the Senate and the Democrats have 49 seats.
sentences.zh: 他现在无法赢得这场争斗的原因是他仍然需要在参议院获得60票，而民主党拥有49个席位。

sentences.en: Next year, they'll have 47 seats.
sentences.zh: 明年，他们将拥有47个席位。

sentences.en: He still can't win in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 他在参议院仍然无法获胜。

sentences.en: Now he doesn't even have the House.
sentences.zh: 现在他甚至连众议院都没有了。

sentences.en: But the fact is he believed the optics.
sentences.zh: 但事实是他相信了视觉效果。

sentences.en: He believed that a knockdown dragout fight with a divided government would look better for him than a knockdown dragout fight with a Republican House and a Republican Senate.
sentences.zh: 他认为与分裂的政府进行一场激烈的争斗，看起来会比与共和党控制的众议院和参议院进行激烈的争斗对他更有利。

sentences.en: So it looks better for the president, even though the chances of actually getting the wall are worse.
sentences.zh: 所以这对总统来说看起来更好，尽管实际上获得建墙资金的机会更糟。

sentences.en: Are far slimmer.
sentences.zh: 要渺茫得多。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So McConnell has put forward this bill.
sentences.zh: 所以麦康奈尔提出了这项法案。

sentences.en: It passes by a healthy margin.
sentences.zh: 它以很大的优势通过了。

sentences.en: It was more than just a healthy margin.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是很大的优势。

sentences.en: This was a voice vote.
sentences.zh: 这是一次口头表决。

sentences.en: This meant they didn't even call a roll call to get people on record.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们甚至没有进行点名表决来记录每个人的立场。

sentences.en: They just said, how do people feel?
sentences.zh: 他们只是问，大家感觉如何？

sentences.en: Yeah, let's pass it.
sentences.zh: 好，我们通过吧。

sentences.en: Anyone against?
sentences.zh: 有人反对吗？

sentences.en: A little bit of grumbling.
sentences.zh: 有一点抱怨声。

sentences.en: But let's just gavel it shut.
sentences.zh: 但我们还是敲槌结案吧。

sentences.en: We're done.
sentences.zh: 我们结束了。

sentences.en: There's no problem here.
sentences.zh: 这里没问题。

sentences.en: So then it was expected to go to the House, which was going to pass it, and then to the president's desk.
sentences.zh: 所以当时预计法案会提交给众议院，众议院会通过，然后送到总统办公桌上。

sentences.en: And he was expected to sign it.
sentences.zh: 而且预计他会签署。

sentences.en: So what exactly changed?
sentences.zh: 那么到底发生了什么变化？

sentences.en: Am I reading it wrong or is that a major, major mistake?
sentences.zh: 是我理解错了，还是这犯了一个极其严重的错误？

sentences.en: No, that's clearly the state of play.
sentences.zh: 不，这就是目前的局势。

sentences.en: In two words, Ann Coulter.
sentences.zh: 用两个词概括：安·库尔特（Ann Coulter）。

sentences.en: The beginning and the end of the problem is Trump.
sentences.zh: 问题的始作俑者和终结者都是特朗普。

sentences.en: He ran on building a wall.
sentences.zh: 他竞选时承诺要建一堵墙。

sentences.en: He's not building the pain.
sentences.zh: 他现在却没在建。

sentences.en: Or he has no earthly idea how to get it done and no interest in finding out.
sentences.zh: 或者说他根本不知道该怎么做，也没兴趣去弄明白。

sentences.en: She said, no, no, we want $5 billion, no less, and we want a wall.
sentences.zh: 她说，不，不，我们要50亿美元，一分都不能少，我们要建墙。

sentences.en: And once he saw them make these demands, suddenly he got squishy.
sentences.zh: 一旦他看到他们提出这些要求，他突然就软了。

sentences.en: And he didn't like the ways out that congressional leaders were trying to offer him.
sentences.zh: 而且他不喜欢国会领袖试图为他提供的脱身方案。

sentences.en: It is becoming clearer and clearer that all we're getting, the wall, the wall, whenever increasingly fewer.
sentences.zh: 越来越清楚的是，我们得到的只有墙，墙，而且支持的人越来越少。

sentences.en: I mean, remember, Ann Coulter is speaking for the people who voted for him on immigration more than anything else.
sentences.zh: 我是说，记住，安·库尔特代表的是那些因为移民问题而投票给特朗普的人，这比什么都重要。

sentences.en: And when she calls him a gutless president presiding over a country without a wall, ouch, that must have hurt.
sentences.zh: 当她称他为一个没有墙的国家里的无胆总统时，哎哟，那一定很伤人。

sentences.en: So this morning, the House Republican conference, those are all the House Republicans, got together to have a meeting.
sentences.zh: 所以今天早上，众议院共和党会议，也就是所有众议院共和党人，聚在一起开了个会。

sentences.en: And Kevin McCarthy, the majority leader, Paul Ryan, the outgoing Speaker of the House, they get up there.
sentences.zh: 多数党领袖凯文·麦卡锡（Kevin McCarthy）和即将离任的众议院议长保罗·瑞安（Paul Ryan）站了起来。

sentences.en: They say, we're putting this bill on the floor.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们要把这个法案提交表决。

sentences.en: You're going to vote for it.
sentences.zh: 你们得投赞成票。

sentences.en: And, you know, all heck breaks loose.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，乱成一团了。

sentences.en: The conservatives start screaming about it.
sentences.zh: 保守派开始大声抗议。

sentences.en: They say, there's no way we can do this.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们绝不可能这么做。

sentences.en: It's going to destroy us.
sentences.zh: 这会毁了我们。

sentences.en: It's going to destroy our base.
sentences.zh: 这会毁了我们的基本盘。

sentences.en: And it's going to destroy Donald Trump because without his base, Trump will have nothing left.
sentences.zh: 这也会毁了唐纳德·特朗普，因为没有了基本盘，特朗普就一无所有了。

sentences.en: And in the middle of this scream fest going on behind closed doors, there's this dramatic moment where Paul Ryan gets a phone call and says, I've got a phone call.
sentences.zh: 在闭门会议的喧闹声中，出现了一个戏剧性的时刻，保罗·瑞安接到了一个电话，说，我接个电话。

sentences.en: It's from Trump.
sentences.zh: 是特朗普打来的。

sentences.en: He storms out of the meeting to take this call from Trump.
sentences.zh: 他冲出会场去接特朗普的电话。

sentences.en: The next thing we hear, there's an emergency meeting with the Republican leadership at the White House to meet about what to do about this wall funding.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们听到的是，共和党领导层在白宫召开紧急会议，商讨如何处理这笔筑墙资金。

sentences.en: And I thought, OK, it might still work out.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，好吧，也许还有转机。

sentences.en: But then when I saw who was on the list at the meeting, I thought, we are dead.
sentences.zh: 但当我看到参会名单时，我想，我们完了。

sentences.en: Who was on the list?
sentences.zh: 名单上都有谁？

sentences.en: Because it wasn't just the leadership.
sentences.zh: 因为不仅仅是领导层。

sentences.en: It also included Jim Jordan and Mark Meadows.
sentences.zh: 还包括吉姆·乔丹（Jim Jordan）和马克·梅多斯（Mark Meadows）。

sentences.en: These were the hardline leaders of the House Freedom Caucus.
sentences.zh: 他们是众议院自由核心小组的强硬派领袖。

sentences.en: And I just imagine them going into the White House and Paul Ryan saying, oh, Mr. President, you have to sign this.
sentences.zh: 我能想象他们走进白宫，保罗·瑞安说，哦，总统先生，您必须签署这个法案。

sentences.en: You can't shut down the government.
sentences.zh: 您不能让政府停摆。

sentences.en: And Jim Jordan and Mark Meadows saying the exact opposite, saying, Mr. President, you have to veto this bill.
sentences.zh: 而吉姆·乔丹和马克·梅多斯则说完全相反的话，说，总统先生，您必须否决这个法案。

sentences.en: And the president gets to hear exactly the message he wants to hear, which is you have the power to stop this.
sentences.zh: 总统听到的正是他想听到的信息，那就是你有权阻止这一切。

sentences.en: So these are basically the Ann Coulters of the House, suddenly in the White House with the president, counseling him on what to do.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人基本上就是众议院里的安·库尔特，突然出现在白宫，给总统出谋划策。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And those were voices that Ryan just couldn't overcome.
sentences.zh: 而这些声音是瑞安无法克服的。

sentences.en: Do a couple of statements and we're just going to go.
sentences.zh: 发表几项声明，我们就要走了。

sentences.en: So after this meeting, Paul Ryan sheepishly emerges from the White House.
sentences.zh: 会议结束后，保罗·瑞安怯生生地从白宫走出来。

sentences.en: He steps to the microphones where the press is gathered and he says,
sentences.zh: 他走到媒体聚集的麦克风前说，

sentences.en: All right, let me just start off right now.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我先从现在开始说起。

sentences.en: We just had a very long, productive meeting with the president.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚与总统进行了一次非常漫长且富有成效的会议。

sentences.en: The president informed us that he will not sign the bill that came up from the Senate last evening because of his legitimate concerns for border security.
sentences.zh: 总统通知我们，由于他对边境安全的合理关切，他不会签署昨晚从参议院提交上来的法案。

sentences.en: The president isn't going to sign this bill.
sentences.zh: 总统不会签署这个法案。

sentences.en: And instead of pushing back on the president, Ryan does what Ryan does.
sentences.zh: 瑞安没有反驳总统，而是做了他一贯的做法。

sentences.en: He says that the president is rightfully concerned about the security of our nation's borders.
sentences.zh: 他说总统对国家边境安全的担忧是正当的。

sentences.en: So he kind of bolstered the president.
sentences.zh: 所以他算是支持了总统。

sentences.en: So what we're going to do is go back to the House and work with our members.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要做的是回到众议院，与我们的成员合作。

sentences.en: We want to keep the government open, but we also want to see an agreement that protects the border.
sentences.zh: 我们希望保持政府运作，但也希望看到一项保护边境的协议。

sentences.en: We have very serious concerns.
sentences.zh: 我们有非常严重的关切。

sentences.en: Now, they do have a plan here, but the plan seems a little cockamamie.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们确实有一个计划，但这个计划看起来有点荒唐。

sentences.en: They're going to go back to the House and they're going to have a vote to bring the stopgap spending bill to the floor,
sentences.zh: 他们要回到众议院，进行投票，将权宜性支出法案提交表决，

sentences.en: then have a vote to add the five billion dollars in wall funding.
sentences.zh: 然后投票增加50亿美元的筑墙资金。

sentences.en: I think what they're actually hoping to happen is that that vote to add the wall funding will fail.
sentences.zh: 我想他们真正希望发生的是，增加筑墙资金的投票会失败。

sentences.en: Then they can go back to the president and say, hey, we did our beSt.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就可以回到总统那里说，嘿，我们尽力了。

sentences.en: We really tried to do what you wanted.
sentences.zh: 我们真的试图做你想要的事。

sentences.en: We just don't have the votes.
sentences.zh: 只是我们票数不够。

sentences.en: And that's where we stand.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的处境。

sentences.en: We're waiting for that vote.
sentences.zh: 我们正在等待那次投票。

sentences.en: So pass a version of the bill that's palatable to the president, but that will fail so that when they go back to the president,
sentences.zh: 所以通过一个总统能接受但会失败的法案版本，这样当他们回到总统那里时，

sentences.en: they have no cards in their hands and he has to accept that this is over, that he is depleted.
sentences.zh: 他们手中没有筹码，他必须接受这一切已经结束，他已经精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: Now, the worst case scenario is actually that the House succeeds in passing a stopgap spending bill into February with the five billion dollars in wall funding.
sentences.zh: 现在，最坏的情况实际上是众议院成功通过了一项包含50亿美元筑墙资金、持续到二月份的权宜性支出法案。

sentences.en: Because if that happens, that bill has to go back to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 因为如果发生这种情况，该法案必须回到参议院。

sentences.en: All the senators are gone.
sentences.zh: 所有的参议员都走了。

sentences.en: Mitch McConnell, the Senate majority leader, has already told the senators, if this bill passes, you guys have to get back on an airplane,
sentences.zh: 参议院多数党领袖米奇·麦康奈尔（Mitch McConnell）已经告诉参议员们，如果这个法案通过，你们必须坐飞机回来，

sentences.en: come back to Washington and vote tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天回到华盛顿投票。

sentences.en: And once again, they don't have the 60 votes.
sentences.zh: 而且再一次，他们没有60票。

sentences.en: It will go down and we will be exactly where we stand now, just hours away from a shutdown.
sentences.zh: 它会被否决，我们将回到现在的处境，距离政府停摆仅剩几个小时。

sentences.en: The scary thing is that if Trump really is watching the end cultures of the world and wanting to satisfy them, he might not blink and reopen the government quickly.
sentences.zh: 可怕的是，如果特朗普真的在关注世界上的安·库尔特们并想满足他们，他可能不会眨眼，也不会很快让政府重新开门。

sentences.en: And the Democrats have absolutely no incentive to do anything until the House turns Democratic in January.
sentences.zh: 而且民主党人完全没有动力在众议院一月份转为民主党控制之前做任何事情。

sentences.en: So if the government shuts down this weekend,
sentences.zh: 所以如果政府这个周末停摆，

sentences.en: much of the government could stay shut down until January 3rd when the Democrats take over the House and promptly pass a bill to open the government and then put it back into Donald Trump's lap.
sentences.zh: 政府的大部分可能会一直停摆到1月3日，届时民主党人将接管众议院，并迅速通过一项法案让政府重新开门，然后把它扔回唐纳德·特朗普的怀里。

sentences.en: And then what will he do?
sentences.zh: 然后他会怎么做？

sentences.en: We have no idea.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: So, Jonathan, if there is, in fact, a government shutdown and it extends through the Christmas holiday, through New Year's, all the way till the Democratic House takes over,
sentences.zh: 那么，乔纳森，如果政府真的停摆，并且持续到圣诞假期、新年，一直到民主党控制众议院，

sentences.en: how do those who advocated for this showdown, like the Ann Coulters and the Mark Meadows and the Jim Jordans, how do they see this benefiting the Republican Party in the long run?
sentences.zh: 那些主张这场对峙的人，比如安·库尔特、马克·梅多斯和吉姆·乔丹，他们如何看待这对共和党长期的好处？

sentences.en: At some point, they're going to have to capitulate, but for now, they want to be able to say, we took it to the mat.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，他们将不得不屈服，但现在，他们想说，我们抗争到底了。

sentences.en: We did everything we possibly could to try to get that $5 billion for this wall.
sentences.zh: 我们尽了最大努力去争取那50亿美元的筑墙费。

sentences.en: We even shut down the government for that $5 billion.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至为了那50亿美元让政府停摆了。

sentences.en: And ultimately, the dastardly Democrats took over the House and what were we going to do?
sentences.zh: 最终，卑鄙的民主党人接管了众议院，我们能怎么办呢？

sentences.en: I want to play kind of devil's advocate politically for just a moment because it feels like what the midterms showed us was that Republicans retained the Senate,
sentences.zh: 我想从政治角度扮演一下魔鬼代言人，因为中期选举似乎向我们表明，共和党保住了参议院，

sentences.en: which very much resembles the Electoral College map of a presidential run, by deploying this strategy, by talking about immigration, by talking about the wall.
sentences.zh: 这非常像总统竞选的选举人团地图，通过部署这一策略，谈论移民，谈论墙。

sentences.en: So is what the president doing essentially activating kind of plan 2020 now?
sentences.zh: 所以总统现在所做的是不是本质上在启动所谓的2020计划？

sentences.en: I think that's true.
sentences.zh: 我认为是真的。

sentences.en: I think that the president is trying to make sure that the rural states are staying in his camp.
sentences.zh: 我认为总统正试图确保农村州留在他的阵营中。

sentences.en: But remember, your account of what happened in the Senate is not all that clean because the Democratic senators who are up for reelection in Wisconsin, in Michigan, and in Ohio,
sentences.zh: 但请记住，你对参议院发生的事情的描述并不完全准确，因为在威斯康星州、密歇根州和俄亥俄州面临连任的民主党参议员，

sentences.en: and in Pennsylvania, four critical states for Trump, they all won reelection easily.
sentences.zh: 以及宾夕法尼亚州，这四个对特朗普至关重要的州，他们都轻松赢得了连任。

sentences.en: So it's not at all clear that in the industrial Midwest, those states that Trump needs so badly, this is even playing that big.
sentences.zh: 所以，在工业中西部，那些特朗普急需的州，这是否真的有那么大的影响，还很不清楚。

sentences.en: So Ann Coulter, in this moment, could be representing a base voter that actually doesn't quite exist and that may not give the president his reelection.
sentences.zh: 所以安·库尔特此刻可能代表了一个实际上并不完全存在的选民基础，这可能无法让总统连任。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Ann Coulter certainly represents a wing of the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 安·库尔特当然代表了共和党的一个派系。

sentences.en: There's no question.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: But I'm not so sure that Ann Coulter speaks to as big a base as Donald Trump thinks she does.
sentences.zh: 但我不太确定安·库尔特所代表的基本盘是否像唐纳德·特朗普认为的那么大。

sentences.en: Okay, Jonathan, I'm going to ask you for your prediction.
sentences.zh: 好的，乔纳森，我要问你的预测。

sentences.en: It is now 5.26 p.m.
sentences.zh: 现在是下午5点26分。

sentences.en: on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 周四。

sentences.en: How do you predict that this year and all of this Mishigas ends?
sentences.zh: 你预测今年和这一切闹剧将如何收场？

sentences.en: I am still predicting that in the end, Donald Trump will sign some kind of spending bill to punt us into next year so we can have this fight with Nancy Pelosi instead of Paul Ryan.
sentences.zh: 我仍然预测，最终，唐纳德·特朗普会签署某种支出法案，把我们推到明年，这样我们就可以和南希·佩洛西（Nancy Pelosi）而不是保罗·瑞安进行这场斗争。

sentences.en: Maybe there will be a short shutdown, but it won't be forever.
sentences.zh: 也许会有短暂的停摆，但不会永远持续下去。

sentences.en: So there's a possibility of a short shutdown, but you believe eventually he will sign some sort of temporary spending bill.
sentences.zh: 所以有可能出现短暂的停摆，但你认为他最终会签署某种临时支出法案。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He probably sees a real benefit in having another one of these fights in February because that's just when the Democrats are going to be wanting to push their own agenda and their own investigative efforts against him.
sentences.zh: 他可能认为在二月份再进行一次这样的斗争有真正的好处，因为那时民主党人正想推动他们自己的议程和针对他的调查工作。

sentences.en: So, hey, at least this is a diversion from that.
sentences.zh: 所以，嘿，至少这可以转移注意力。

sentences.en: Well, as the politics editor in Washington, what does it mean to you to carry a fight like this into the new year?
sentences.zh: 那么，作为华盛顿的政治编辑，把这样的斗争带入新的一年对你意味着什么？

sentences.en: Not exactly a fresh start.
sentences.zh: 这可不是一个全新的开始。

sentences.en: What does that tell you looking ahead to 2019?
sentences.zh: 展望2019年，这说明了什么？

sentences.en: I think that tells me that we won't be getting a fresh break with a democratically controlled house.
sentences.zh: 我认为这说明我们不会在民主党控制的众议院下获得一个全新的转机。

sentences.en: We're going to have a lot of lingering fights going on.
sentences.zh: 我们将会有很多悬而未决的斗争。

sentences.en: And I think that the Democrats will be as frustrated about that as any Republican because the fact is the Democrats have an agenda and they want to be focusing on that.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为民主党人会和任何共和党人一样对此感到沮丧，因为事实是民主党人有自己的议程，他们想专注于此。

sentences.en: They don't want to have to be responding to Donald Trump's provocations.
sentences.zh: 他们不想被迫回应唐纳德·特朗普的挑衅。

sentences.en: And this will be a chance for Donald Trump to once again grab the microphone and start screaming about a wall.
sentences.zh: 这将是唐纳德·特朗普再次抢过麦克风，开始大喊大叫关于墙的机会。

sentences.en: Jonathan, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 乔纳森，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Cheers.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: On Thursday night, the House passed a bill that would fund President Trump's border wall.
sentences.zh: 周四晚上，众议院通过了一项为特朗普总统的边境墙提供资金的法案。

sentences.en: That bill now heads to the Senate, where it is expected to be voted down.
sentences.zh: 该法案现在提交给参议院，预计将被否决。

sentences.en: Look at this.
sentences.zh: 看这个。

sentences.en: The news just broke that Jim Mattis is leaving.
sentences.zh: 刚刚传出消息，吉姆·马蒂斯（Jim Mattis）要离职了。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Yeah, he just tweeted it.
sentences.zh: 是的，他刚发了推文。

sentences.en: General Jim Mattis will be retiring with distinction at the end of February after serving in my administration as Secretary of Defense.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·马蒂斯将军将在二月底光荣退休，此前他在我的政府中担任国防部长。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能获取所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且不需要输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间去深入了解《时报》订阅者每天都能看到的内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他事情。

sentences.en: In his resignation letter to the President, Mattis emphasized the need to respect allies and identify enemies,
sentences.zh: 在给总统的辞职信中，马蒂斯强调了尊重盟友和识别敌人的必要性，

sentences.en: concluding that Trump deserves a Secretary of Defense whose views are, quote, better aligned with yours, on these and other issues.
sentences.zh: 并总结说，特朗普应该拥有一位在这些问题和其他问题上，引用他的话，“与你的观点更一致”的国防部长。

sentences.en: And…
sentences.zh: 还有……

sentences.en: During his annual press conference in Moscow, Russian President Vladimir Putin praised Trump's decision to withdraw troops from Syria,
sentences.zh: 在莫斯科举行的年度新闻发布会上，俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京赞扬了特朗普从叙利亚撤军的决定，

sentences.en: saying American soldiers were no longer needed there.
sentences.zh: 称美国士兵在那里已不再需要。

sentences.en: Putin's remarks seemed to fulfill the worry of U.S.
sentences.zh: 普京的言论似乎印证了美国军方领导人的担忧，

sentences.en: military leaders, including Mattis, that Trump's decision would cede influence in Syria to U.S.
sentences.zh: 包括马蒂斯在内的军方领导人担心，特朗普的决定会将叙利亚的影响力拱手让给美国的

sentences.en: adversaries, including Russia and Iran, to the detriment of U.S.
sentences.zh: 对手，包括俄罗斯和伊朗，从而损害美国的

sentences.en: interests.
sentences.zh: 利益。

sentences.en: The Daily is produced by Theo Balcom, Lindsay Garrison, Rachel Quester, Annie Brown, Andy Mills, Ike Srees-Kamiraja, Claire Tennesketter, Michael Simon-Johnson, Jessica Chung,
sentences.zh: 《每日新闻》由西奥·巴尔科姆、琳赛·加里森、雷切尔·奎斯特、安妮·布朗、安迪·米尔斯、艾克·斯里斯-卡米拉贾、克莱尔·坦内斯凯特、迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊、杰西卡·钟制作，

sentences.en: Alexandra Lee Young, and Jonathan Wolfe, and edited by Paige Cowan, Larissa Anderson, and Wendy Doerr.
sentences.zh: 亚历山德拉·李·杨和乔纳森·沃尔夫制作，并由佩奇·考恩、拉丽莎·安德森和温迪·多尔编辑。

sentences.en: Lisa Tobin is our executive producer, Samantha Hennig is our editorial director, our technical manager is Brad Fisher, our engineer is Chris Wood,
sentences.zh: 丽莎·托宾是我们的执行制片人，萨曼莎·亨尼格是我们的编辑总监，技术经理是布拉德·费舍尔，工程师是克里斯·伍德，

sentences.en: and our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Sam Dolnick, Michaela Bouchard, and Stella Tan.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢萨姆·多尔尼克、米凯拉·布沙尔和斯特拉·谭。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: Next week, our second annual Year in Sound, and we'll hear updates from some of our favorite stories of the year.
sentences.zh: 下周，我们将播出第二届年度“声音之年”特辑，届时我们将听到今年一些热门报道的后续进展。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为您准备假期接待客人的相关内容。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人们宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们需要全黑的睡眠环境吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝断片了才去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这可是非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 您可以在《纽约时报》应用程序或您喜欢的任何播客平台收听《Wirecutter秀》。
